messages:
jess: heads-up — noticed a spike in runtime NaNs hitting the pos-enc kernel on nightly cluster runs :eyes:
sam: ugh, link to failing job?
jess: https://ci.internal/redwood/builds/12458 logs show `attn_bias` accumulation going NaN inside alibi kernel for quantized int8 path
liam: is this the new kernel selector change from the RFC?
jess: yes — selector prefers the 'quantized-alibi' kernel when model is int8 and seq_len > 1024
rachel: quick hypothesis: we might be doing inplace accumulation with reduced precision, and the clamp/scale step is lost in some codepaths
liam: can repro locally with a minimal loop: ```python
for t in range(seq):
  bias += alibi_step(t)  # in int8 path we upcast later -> overflow
```
liam: reproduces on CUDA compute 8.6 with our optimized kernels
matt: from infra side, failure correlates with larger batch sizes and short warmup — fewer fp32 fallbacks
ops-bot: CI alert: failing tests marked flakiness=high for build 12458 (added by jess)
sam: we need two things: 1) short-term mitigation to avoid customer impact 2) API/refactor to prevent future subtle precision bugs
rachel: for mitigation: force float32 accumulation for bias regardless of weight quantization. cheap and safe
liam: agree. We can add a guarded upcast in kernel entry: `bias_accum = float32(bias_accum)` before add loop. minimal perf hit.
jess: +1. Also would like a canary flag so Dedicated customers with strict latency can opt-in to old selector while we stabilize
matt: canary route is possible at routing layer. ops: add rollout flag `posenc_stable_fallback` scoped to customer/region
ops-bot: Action logged: created rollout flag `posenc_stable_fallback` (owner: matt)
sam: for long-term: propose refactor in kernel API boundary — two separate responsibilities: (A) position encoding value compute (pure, deterministic float32 math) (B) memory layout / quantized encode mapper (no math). Put accumulation in A so it is always in fp32; B only does packing/format
rachel: that separation makes sense. Also helps testing: A can be unit-tested with high-precision golden outputs
liam: downside: extra copy/convert step before packing, but we can fuse on hot path if packing supports `pack_from_fp32`
jess: also add a fuzz test in eval harness that randomizes seq_len, batch, and quant params to catch regressions early
sam: agree. I'll draft a follow-up RFC addendum: kernel API: `compute_posenc_fp32(ctx, seq_len) -> fp32_buffer` and `pack_posenc(buffer, quant_mode) -> device_buffer` plus canonical tests
matt: timeline?
sam: mitigation PR today (small guarded upcast). RFC addendum draft by EOD. canary rollout next week.
jess: I'll open the PR and link in thread
ops-bot: PR created: https://git.internal/redwood/infra/PR/3001 by jess
liam: once PR lands let's add microbench comparing pure-fp32 vs fp32->pack on our perf harness (measure latency P50/P95)
rachel: also note for ALiBi we should avoid cumulative sums that grow with seq_len in quant path — prefer per-step local offsets + stable subtraction trick
sam: good call. will include numeric-stability section in RFC addendum
jess: thanks everyone. feel free to DM if you want to pair on reproducer. :thumbsup:
